questions.question: How many players from each team are allowed on the ice during regular play?
questions.hint: Think about how many positions there are: forwards and defense plus one more special player.
questions.explanation: Each team has 6 players on ice: 3 forwards, 2 defensemen, and 1 goalie.

questions.question: A player can score a goal with their skate.
questions.hint: As long as there's no kicking motion, goals can be scored off any part of the body!
questions.explanation: Goals can be scored off skates as long as there's no distinct kicking motion.

questions.question: How long is a minor penalty?
questions.hint: It's shorter than a major penalty but longer than a minute.
questions.explanation: Minor penalties are 2 minutes long.

questions.question: What is it called when a player shoots the puck from behind center ice past the opponent's goal line?
questions.hint: It rhymes with 'slicing' and stops play.
questions.explanation: Icing occurs when the puck crosses the goal line after being shot from behind center.

questions.question: What happens when a team gets a penalty?
questions.hint: The penalized player has to sit in a special box.
questions.explanation: When a team gets a penalty, they play shorthanded while the player serves time in the penalty box.

questions.question: Offside happens when a player enters the offensive zone before the puck.
questions.hint: The puck needs to be first across the blue line!
questions.explanation: Offside occurs when an attacking player crosses the blue line before the puck.

questions.question: What is a power play?
options: When one team has more players on ice
questions.correctAnswer: When one team has more players on ice
questions.hint: It happens when the other team has a penalty.
questions.explanation: A power play occurs when one team has more players on ice due to opponent penalties.

questions.question: What do we call the area in front of the goal where the goalie plays?
questions.hint: It's painted blue and only the goalie should be there.
questions.explanation: The crease is the semi-circular area in front of the goal.

questions.question: How many periods are in a hockey game?
questions.hint: Same as the number of forwards on the ice!
questions.explanation: Hockey games have 3 periods of play.

questions.question: A goalie can play the puck anywhere on the ice.
questions.hint: There's a special area behind the net where goalies can't play the puck.
questions.explanation: Goalies cannot play the puck in the trapezoid corners behind the net.

questions.question: What is a hat trick?
questions.hint: Fans throw hats on the ice when this happens!
questions.explanation: A hat trick is when one player scores 3 goals in a single game.

questions.question: What penalty is called for hitting an opponent with your stick?
questions.hint: The word describes a swinging motion with a stick.
questions.explanation: Slashing is called when a player swings their stick at an opponent.

questions.question: Fighting is allowed in hockey without any penalties.
questions.hint: Players who fight get sent to the penalty box!
questions.explanation: Fighting results in major penalties for both players involved.

questions.question: How long is each period in youth hockey?
questions.hint: It's shorter than NHL games but longer than 10 minutes.
questions.explanation: Youth hockey periods are typically 15 minutes long.

questions.question: What do we call it when a team pulls their goalie for an extra attacker?
questions.hint: The net has nobody guarding it!
questions.explanation: An empty net situation occurs when a team removes their goalie for an extra skater.

questions.question: In our 2-1-2 forecheck, how many forwards pressure in the offensive zone?
questions.hint: Look at the first number in '2-1-2'.
questions.explanation: In a 2-1-2 forecheck, 2 forwards apply pressure deep in the offensive zone.

questions.question: On a breakout, the defensemen should always pass up the middle.
questions.hint: Using the boards is often safer!
questions.explanation: Defensemen should use the boards and wings for safer breakout passes.

questions.question: Where should the center position themselves on a defensive zone faceoff?
questions.hint: The center takes the faceoff!
questions.explanation: The center takes faceoffs at the dot while other players position around them.

questions.question: What formation do we use on the power play?
questions.hint: It's shaped like something you use in the rain.
questions.explanation: The umbrella formation has one player up high and players spread around the zone.

questions.question: On a 2-on-1 rush, what should the defenseman do?
options: Cover the player without the puck
questions.hint: Position yourself to take away the passing lane while still being able to pressure the shooter!
questions.explanation: The defenseman should stay in the middle to take away the pass option while still being able to challenge the shooter if needed.

questions.question: Wingers should stay on their strong side during breakouts.
questions.hint: It's easier to receive passes on your forehand!
questions.explanation: Wingers should stay on their strong side for better puck control on breakouts.

questions.question: What's the first option on our breakout?
questions.hint: The boards are your friend on breakouts!
questions.explanation: The first breakout option is typically a pass to the winger along the boards.

questions.question: What defensive system do we use in our own zone?
questions.hint: Four players make a shape, one roams.
questions.explanation: Box plus one has 4 players in a box formation with one player pressuring the puck.

questions.question: On the penalty kill, how many players should pressure the puck carrier?
questions.hint: Too many chasers leave gaps!
questions.explanation: One player pressures while others maintain defensive positioning.

questions.question: The weak side winger should always crash the net on offensive zone entries.
questions.hint: Going to the net creates scoring chances!
questions.explanation: The weak side winger driving the net creates screens and rebound opportunities.

questions.question: Which team has won the most Stanley Cups?
questions.hint: They're from Quebec and have won it 24 times!
questions.explanation: The Montreal Canadiens have won 24 Stanley Cups, the most in NHL history.

questions.question: Wayne Gretzky wore number 99.
questions.hint: His number is retired league-wide!
questions.explanation: Wayne Gretzky wore 99, which is now retired across the entire NHL.

questions.question: What team does Connor McDavid play for?
questions.hint: They're from Alberta and wear blue and orange!
questions.explanation: Connor McDavid is the captain of the Edmonton Oilers.

questions.question: What trophy is awarded to the NHL's best goalie?
questions.hint: It starts with a 'V'.
questions.explanation: The Vezina Trophy is awarded annually to the NHL's best goaltender.

questions.question: How many teams are in the NHL?
questions.hint: Seattle and Vegas are the newest teams!
questions.explanation: There are 32 teams in the NHL as of the 2021-22 season.

questions.question: The Toronto Maple Leafs last won the Stanley Cup in 1967.
questions.hint: It's been a very long time for Leafs fans!
questions.explanation: The Maple Leafs' last Stanley Cup win was in 1967.

questions.question: Which player is known as 'The Great One'?
questions.hint: He has more assists than any other player has total points!
questions.explanation: Wayne Gretzky is known as 'The Great One' for his incredible career achievements.

questions.question: What team is known as the 'Habs'?
questions.hint: They're from Quebec and have the most championships.
questions.explanation: The Montreal Canadiens are nicknamed the 'Habs' short for 'Les Habitants'.

questions.question: What should you always check before stepping on the ice?
questions.hint: Safety first - protect your head!
questions.explanation: Always ensure your helmet is properly secured before playing.

questions.question: How often should you sharpen your skates?
questions.hint: It depends on how much you skate!
questions.explanation: Skates typically need sharpening every 10-15 hours of ice time.

questions.question: What protects your neck from skate cuts?
questions.hint: It wraps around your neck area.
questions.explanation: A neck guard protects against potential skate blade injuries.

questions.question: What should you do if your equipment gets damaged during a game?
questions.hint: Safety is the top priority!
questions.explanation: Always inform coaches about damaged equipment for your safety.

questions.question: What should you do after every game, win or lose?
questions.hint: It's about respect!
questions.explanation: The handshake line shows respect for opponents regardless of the outcome.

questions.question: What's the Thunder team motto?
options: Have fun, work hard, be respectful
questions.correctAnswer: Have fun, work hard, be respectful
questions.hint: It's about more than just winning!
questions.explanation: The Thunder values fun, hard work, and respect above all.

questions.question: Thunder players should help opponents up after a collision.
questions.hint: Good sportsmanship means respecting everyone!
questions.explanation: Helping opponents up demonstrates excellent sportsmanship.

questions.question: In Thunder's Defensive Zone Coverage, what shape do the 5 players form to protect our net?
questions.hint: Think about how dots are arranged on dice!
questions.explanation: The Thunder Box uses a '5 on a die' formation - everyone stays between their man and our net.

questions.question: What's the nickname for Thunder's offensive forecheck system?
questions.hint: One player goes to get it, one supports - like a famous duo!
questions.explanation: Batman & Robin Forecheck: Batman goes to get the puck, Robin supports.

questions.question: In corner battles, what does the first Thunder player do?
questions.hint: They apply force on the opponent!
questions.explanation: First player pressures, second player supports - Thunder Wall system.

questions.question: What's Thunder's main goal on breakouts?
questions.hint: Thunder Strike Exit - we want speed!
questions.explanation: Get the puck out of our zone fast and clean - Thunder Strike Exit.

questions.question: On zone entries, Thunder players should spread out to create space before attacking.
questions.hint: Space first, then speed!
questions.explanation: Thunder Strike Entry: Create space by spreading out, then attack with speed and purpose.

questions.question: When defending the rush, Thunder players should force opponents to go where?
questions.hint: Never through the middle!
questions.explanation: Thunder Shield: Close the gap, angle them off, make them beat us wide - never through the middle!

questions.question: What are Thunder's three team values? (Answer: Fast, Smart, ___)
questions.hint: We play as a team!
questions.explanation: Thunder values: Fast, Smart, Together!

questions.question: At the blue lines, what should Thunder players do if there's traffic?
options: Chip it out or dump it in
questions.correctAnswer: Chip it out or dump it in
questions.hint: Make smart decisions, don't force it!
questions.explanation: Blue Line Boss: Make smart decisions - chip it out or dump it in, don't dangle through traffic!

questions.question: Thunder's goalie positioning rule: Stay ready, track the puck, challenge shooters.
questions.hint: Thunder's Last Line!
questions.explanation: Goaltending: Stay ready, track the puck, challenge shooters, and remember - your team has your back!

questions.question: What is Thunder's team promise?
options: We bring the storm every shift, every game
questions.correctAnswer: We bring the storm every shift, every game
questions.hint: It's about effort, not just winning!
questions.explanation: Our Promise: We bring the storm every shift, every game!

questions.question: Thunder players should only work hard when winning.
questions.hint: Every shift, every game!
questions.explanation: Thunder Way means bringing maximum effort every shift, regardless of the score.

questions.question: What zone does the Thunder Wall protect?
questions.hint: We protect our house!
questions.explanation: Thunder Wall is our defensive zone coverage system.

questions.question: In the Batman & Robin forecheck, who goes to get the puck?
questions.hint: The main hero goes first!
questions.explanation: Batman goes to get the puck, Robin provides support.

questions.question: How should Thunder players treat their teammates after a mistake?
questions.hint: Together is one of our values!
questions.explanation: Thunder value 'Together' means supporting teammates through good and bad.

questions.question: When passing while skating, where should you aim the puck?
questions.hint: Lead your teammate in the direction they're skating!
questions.explanation: Pass ahead of the receiver so they can catch it in stride without slowing down.

questions.question: What's the best way to protect the puck from an opponent?
options: Hold your stick with one hand
Use your body as a shield
questions.correctAnswer: Use your body as a shield
questions.hint: Your body is bigger than your stick!
questions.explanation: Use your body positioning to shield the puck from defenders.

questions.question: In small area games, what's the main benefit for players?
questions.hint: It's about getting more involved!
questions.explanation: Small area games give players more puck touches and decision-making opportunities.

questions.question: What's a 1-2-2 forecheck?
questions.hint: It's about layers of pressure!
questions.explanation: 1-2-2 means one forward pressures, two support, and two defensemen stay back.

questions.question: When forechecking, the first forward should _____ the puck carrier.
questions.hint: Force them to make a decision!
questions.explanation: The first forechecker angles the puck carrier to force them toward support.

questions.question: In U10 hockey, body checking is allowed.
questions.hint: Safety first for younger players!
questions.explanation: Body checking is not permitted in U10 hockey - only incidental body contact.

questions.question: When is icing NOT called?
questions.hint: It helps the team that's down a player!
questions.explanation: Teams on penalty kill can ice the puck without penalty.

questions.question: For backward skating, what shape should your cuts make?
questions.hint: Think of the letter shape your skates make!
questions.explanation: C-cuts provide the best propulsion for backward skating.

questions.question: A backhand pass is usually less accurate than a forehand pass.
questions.hint: With practice, both can be equally good!
questions.explanation: Backhand passes can be just as accurate with proper technique.

questions.question: In defensive zone coverage, where should the center typically position?
questions.hint: Protect the most dangerous area!
questions.explanation: Centers typically cover the slot area in front of the net.

questions.question: What do you call it when a player scores three goals in one game?
questions.hint: Fans might throw something on the ice!
questions.explanation: A hat trick is three goals by one player in a single game.

questions.question: The Zamboni machine was invented by Frank Zamboni.
questions.hint: Sometimes things are named after their inventors!
questions.explanation: Frank Zamboni invented the ice resurfacing machine in 1949.

questions.question: When receiving a pass, you should '______' the puck with your stick.
questions.hint: Be soft with it!
questions.explanation: Cushioning the puck helps control it when receiving a pass.

questions.question: What's the ideal length for a drill station at U10 practice?
questions.hint: Long enough to learn, short enough to stay focused!
questions.explanation: 5-7 minutes per station keeps players engaged and allows skill repetition.

questions.question: On a 2-on-1 rush, the puck carrier should always shoot.
questions.hint: What about your teammate?
questions.explanation: On a 2-on-1, read the defender - pass if they commit to you, shoot if they cover the pass.

questions.question: What's the key to a good wrist shot?
questions.hint: Don't give the goalie time!
questions.explanation: A quick release on a wrist shot gives the goalie less time to react.

questions.question: What happens if you shoot the puck over the glass in your defensive zone?
questions.hint: It's an automatic penalty!
questions.explanation: Shooting the puck over the glass from your defensive zone is a 2-minute delay of game penalty.

questions.question: Good teammates _______ each other after mistakes.
questions.hint: Be positive!
questions.explanation: Encouraging teammates after mistakes builds team unity and confidence.

questions.question: In a box penalty kill formation, how many players form the 'box'?
questions.hint: It's called a 'box' for a reason - think about the shape!
questions.explanation: Four penalty killers form a box shape to protect the slot area.

questions.question: What's the advantage of a 5-on-3 power play?
questions.hint: Count the difference in players!
questions.explanation: 5-on-3 means you have two more attackers than defenders, creating lots of space.

questions.question: What type of penalty results in a player being ejected from the game?
questions.hint: It 'matches' the severity - you're out!
questions.explanation: A match penalty means immediate ejection from the game.

questions.question: In a diamond penalty kill, the formation looks like what shape?
questions.hint: The answer is in the name!
questions.explanation: The diamond PK has one player up high, two in the middle, and one low.

questions.question: A team can 'pull' their goalie to add an extra attacker even when not behind.
questions.hint: Strategy isn't just for when you're losing!
questions.explanation: Teams can pull the goalie anytime, like on a delayed penalty call.

questions.question: What's a 'wedge' penalty kill designed to do?
questions.hint: Think about what a wedge shape does - it splits things!
questions.explanation: The wedge PK uses a triangle to force the power play to one side of the ice.

questions.question: What's a 'Michigan' move in hockey?
questions.hint: It's named after a university team that made it famous!
questions.explanation: The Michigan is when you scoop the puck on your stick like lacrosse and score.

questions.question: Which NHL trophy is awarded to the best defensive forward?
questions.hint: It's not for defensemen, but for forwards who play great defense!
questions.explanation: The Frank J. Selke Trophy goes to the forward with the best defensive skills.

questions.question: How many minutes is a double minor penalty?
questions.hint: It's double a regular minor!
questions.explanation: A double minor is 4 minutes (2+2), often given for high-sticking that draws blood.

questions.question: In a 1-3-1 power play, there are three players across the middle of the zone.
questions.hint: The numbers tell you the formation!
questions.explanation: 1-3-1 means 1 up high, 3 across the middle, and 1 down low.

questions.question: A penalty shot is awarded when a player is fouled on a _______.
questions.hint: When you're all alone with the goalie!
questions.explanation: Penalty shots are awarded when fouled on a clear breakaway opportunity.

questions.question: What's the 'Forsberg move' named after Peter Forsberg?
questions.hint: He did it in the Olympics with one hand on his stick!
questions.explanation: The Forsberg is a one-handed deke move made famous in shootouts.

questions.question: What does 'cycling' mean in the offensive zone?
questions.hint: The puck moves in a cycle pattern!
questions.explanation: Cycling means moving the puck along the boards to maintain possession.

questions.question: What's a 'Gordie Howe hat trick'?
questions.hint: Named after 'Mr. Hockey' who could do it all!
questions.explanation: A Gordie Howe hat trick is scoring a goal, an assist, and getting in a fight.

questions.question: Too many men on the ice is always a 2-minute penalty, even in overtime.
questions.hint: The rules don't change for this one!
questions.explanation: Too many men is always a 2-minute minor penalty, regardless of game situation.

questions.question: Where does the faceoff happen after an icing call?
options: Defensive zone of team that iced
questions.correctAnswer: Defensive zone of team that iced
questions.hint: It's a punishment for icing!
questions.explanation: After icing, the faceoff is in the defensive zone of the team that iced the puck.

questions.question: On defensive zone faceoffs, the home team gets to put their stick down last.
questions.hint: Home ice advantage!
questions.explanation: The home team center puts their stick down second, giving them a slight advantage.

questions.question: What type of shot has the quickest release?
questions.hint: It's all in the name - quick like a snap!
questions.explanation: The snap shot combines power and quick release, faster than a wrist shot.

questions.question: When shooting, you should keep your eyes on the _______.
questions.hint: Look where you want the puck to go!
questions.explanation: Always keep your eyes on your target when shooting for better accuracy.

questions.question: How many teams are in the NHL?
questions.hint: It's an even number that divides into 4 divisions!
questions.explanation: The NHL has 32 teams divided into 4 divisions.

questions.question: Wayne Gretzky is known as 'The Great One'.
questions.hint: He holds the most records!
questions.explanation: Wayne Gretzky earned the nickname 'The Great One' for his incredible career.

questions.question: In the last minute of a game when trailing by one, what do teams often do?
questions.hint: More attackers might help score!
questions.explanation: Teams pull their goalie for an extra attacker when trailing late in the game.
